initial: A sanctions entry identifies a person, entity or vessel and the restriction was in force on the relevant date.
expected: A dated award or assistance record can establish a public financial relationship; inspect whether an action actually created obligations, deliveries or payments.
basis: Public money reaching a restricted counterparty is consequential if the applicable restriction reaches the specific conduct. Award records alone are not payment evidence.
outcome: New positive action after the relevant restriction merits an underlying-document check. Zero-dollar closeouts and termination actions do not show continued payments.
ordinary: Closeout; termination; refunds; pre-existing obligations; humanitarian or other authorization; same-name recipient.
disqualifiers: First resolve actual identity and entity type; distinguish SDN blocking from non-SDN restrictions; establish the applicable jurisdiction, conduct, dates, program and authorizations/exceptions. A match alone establishes none of these.
evidence: Designation history, complete award modifications, recipient registration, performance and payment records, program rules and licenses.
next_check: Open one award action and read its description, amount type and effective date before expanding the match.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A sanctions entry identifies a person, entity or vessel and the restriction was in force on the relevant date.
expected: The ownership source may show a dated path to another legal entity; retrieve the underlying ownership evidence and percentages.
basis: Ownership can identify assets and counterparties omitted from a name screen. OFAC automatic blocking requires its actual ownership rule; parent/control labels alone cannot establish it.
outcome: A corroborated ownership chain points to a specific unlisted entity for legal and asset tracing review.
ordinary: Historic ownership; minority interest; control without ownership; reporting exemption; different person.
disqualifiers: First resolve actual identity and entity type; distinguish SDN blocking from non-SDN restrictions; establish the applicable jurisdiction, conduct, dates, program and authorizations/exceptions. A match alone establishes none of these. Do not multiply percentages along arbitrary paths or infer shares from directorship.
evidence: Dated share register, identity evidence, each intermediate owner, share class and aggregation without double counting.
next_check: Read one ownership edge; establish whether it reports ownership, accounting consolidation, control, or merely an officer role.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A sanctions entry identifies a person, entity or vessel and the restriction was in force on the relevant date.
expected: An asset or licence record may identify the same party as holder, operator, proprietor or payment counterparty.
basis: A disclosed asset or operating right offers a concrete way to investigate the reach and implementation of restrictions; registration can persist lawfully while assets are frozen.
outcome: A dated new transfer, renewal or operational relationship after listing warrants document review.
ordinary: Frozen asset retained on register; old owner; operator differs from owner; permission; ordinary remediation.
disqualifiers: First resolve actual identity and entity type; distinguish SDN blocking from non-SDN restrictions; establish the applicable jurisdiction, conduct, dates, program and authorizations/exceptions. A match alone establishes none of these. Registration is not proof of use, transfer, or ability to dispose.
evidence: Title/licence history, role of each party, underlying instrument, restrictions and authorizations.
next_check: Read one asset record and its ownership/holder effective date; distinguish owner from operator.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A sanctions entry identifies a person, entity or vessel and the restriction was in force on the relevant date.
expected: A vessel identity can be followed to dated movement, inspection, detention or registration records.
basis: Movement or port inspection establishes an investigative event, not prohibited trade. Vessel identity persists across many name and flag changes.
outcome: Verified vessel activity in a jurisdiction where a specific restriction may apply merits a cargo and port-document check.
ordinary: Safety entry; rescue; authorized call; stale AIS; spoofed MMSI; inspection without trading.
disqualifiers: First resolve actual identity and entity type; distinguish SDN blocking from non-SDN restrictions; establish the applicable jurisdiction, conduct, dates, program and authorizations/exceptions. A match alone establishes none of these. A vessel track cannot identify cargo or its payer.
evidence: IMO confirmation where present, timestamp provenance, port record, cargo documents, ownership history and applicable restriction.
next_check: Compare IMO numbers first; if unavailable establish a documented vessel-name/registration crosswalk.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A sanctions entry identifies a person, entity or vessel and the restriction was in force on the relevant date.
expected: A disclosure may identify the listed party as a client or foreign principal during a dated engagement.
basis: Representation of a restricted interest can be newsworthy while lawful; disclosure and sanctions rules have different scope.
outcome: An active representation or reported payment after listing justifies checking purpose, authorization and public decision sought.
ordinary: Authorized legal representation; historical filing; termination; namesake; agent is not principal.
disqualifiers: First resolve actual identity and entity type; distinguish SDN blocking from non-SDN restrictions; establish the applicable jurisdiction, conduct, dates, program and authorizations/exceptions. A match alone establishes none of these. Representation alone does not establish illegal lobbying or prohibited payment.
evidence: Engagement dates, principal identity, original disclosure, payment evidence and authorization.
next_check: Read the disclosed client/principal role and amendment history.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A sanctions entry identifies a person, entity or vessel and the restriction was in force on the relevant date.
expected: A contribution record may identify the same individual or entity as donor within the relevant period.
basis: A verified contribution creates a public influence question. Donor eligibility is jurisdiction-specific and has not been legally established here.
outcome: A confirmed donor and dated contribution warrant eligibility, refund and applicable restriction checks.
ordinary: Namesake; employer name mistaken for donor; refunded gift; donation before listing.
disqualifiers: First resolve actual identity and entity type; distinguish SDN blocking from non-SDN restrictions; establish the applicable jurisdiction, conduct, dates, program and authorizations/exceptions. A match alone establishes none of these. No foreign-donor prohibition is presumed without current jurisdiction-specific authority.
evidence: Donor identity, original contribution, amendments/refunds, citizenship or incorporation evidence where legally relevant.
next_check: Check whether the matching field names the donor or only the donor’s employer.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A sanctions entry identifies a person, entity or vessel and the restriction was in force on the relevant date.
expected: An issuer filing may identify the same entity or a documented relationship involving it.
basis: Securities filings can expose material commercial relationships; mere mention does not establish an investment or restricted transaction.
outcome: A dated material holding or transaction involving the listed party merits review of the precise instrument and restriction.
ordinary: Risk-factor mention; divestment; historic subsidiary; unrelated ticker; authorized holding.
disqualifiers: First resolve actual identity and entity type; distinguish SDN blocking from non-SDN restrictions; establish the applicable jurisdiction, conduct, dates, program and authorizations/exceptions. A match alone establishes none of these. Filing date differs from transaction date; disclosure can describe cessation.
evidence: Full filing, transaction terms, issuer identifiers, ownership dates, instrument-level restriction and exceptions.
next_check: Locate the matching passage and determine whether it describes actual business, a risk, or a termination.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A sanctions entry identifies a person, entity or vessel and the restriction was in force on the relevant date.
expected: A charity filing may name the same party as officer, contractor, donor where disclosed, or grantee.
basis: A documented financial or governance role is a tractable public-interest lead; humanitarian work may be authorized.
outcome: A verified transfer or continuing governance role merits checking the legal entity, role and dates.
ordinary: Humanitarian authorization; non-cash disclosure; former officer; common name; distinct grantee branch.
disqualifiers: First resolve actual identity and entity type; distinguish SDN blocking from non-SDN restrictions; establish the applicable jurisdiction, conduct, dates, program and authorizations/exceptions. A match alone establishes none of these.
evidence: Complete filing schedules, actual transfer records, role dates and licenses.
next_check: Read the schedule and confirm which party paid whom.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A named firm/person has an effective ineligibility interval in a development-bank record.
expected: An award record can be tested for identity and whether the award falls within the sanction’s institution, project and procurement scope.
basis: Debarment may constrain particular financed procurement; this run does not establish cross-debarment or universal exclusion rules.
outcome: A dated award in the applicable scope would warrant checking the procurement decision and any exception.
ordinary: Unrelated government award; expired sanction; conditional eligibility; namesake; award before exclusion.
disqualifiers: Do not apply a bank’s debarment universally; obtain current governing rule and project financing before claiming breach.
evidence: Debarment decision, procurement financing and rules, contract date, recipient ID and exception.
next_check: Read the original sanction decision and identify covered institutions and dates.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A record documents a specific enforcement finding, settlement or incident involving an operator.
expected: Later public funding may go to the same legal entity or a demonstrably connected successor.
basis: Repeat public funding can reveal policy choices or monitoring gaps; penalties rarely imply automatic exclusion.
outcome: A material post-finding award with a relevant risk warrants checking due diligence and corrective conditions.
ordinary: Remediation funding; settlement without admission; different subsidiary; lawful eligible supplier.
disqualifiers: Separate allegations from final findings; do not assume debarment or unresolved violation.
evidence: Original finding, disposition, award scope, recipient registration, corrective conditions.
next_check: Read one finding and one award scope to see whether the same risk is implicated.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A procurement dataset identifies award recipients within a defined buyer, market and period.
expected: Distinct recipient IDs may trace to a shared ultimate owner at award time.
basis: Common control can reduce the apparent diversity of suppliers; shared ownership is not bid rigging.
outcome: Concentration under common ownership materially exceeds the count of nominal suppliers.
ordinary: Framework lots; mergers after award; reseller networks; common professional agent.
disqualifiers: Officer/address overlap alone is not common ownership; count unique awards once, separate amendments.
evidence: Recipient registration crosswalk, ownership shares at award date, comparable award amounts.
next_check: Resolve the two largest recipients before building the full ownership graph.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: An award identifies a supplier and a dated procurement decision.
expected: A verified supplier or officer identity may also appear as contributor before the decision.
basis: Timing and money create a question about access or influence, not a causal finding.
outcome: Repeated aligned donations and awards deserve comparison with non-donor suppliers and procurement rules.
ordinary: Legal giving; incumbency; large firm market share; donation after award; donor’s employer only.
disqualifiers: An individual donation cannot be attributed to a company from employer text alone; define comparable opportunity set.
evidence: Award decision date, donor identity/role dates, contribution/refund record, tender competition.
next_check: Check one donor’s relationship to the supplier at the donation date.
temporal: Use contribution dates before a specified procurement decision; compare a prespecified opportunity window and comparable non-donors.

initial: A supplier wins a contract in a defined policy or product area.
expected: Lobbying disclosures may identify that supplier as client and the relevant issue before award.
basis: Lobbying is normally lawful. Disclosed access plus procurement outcomes can guide a focused accountability question.
outcome: Relevant dated engagement and unusual procurement terms warrant checking meeting records and tender rationale.
ordinary: Routine sector lobbying; different issue; reporting lag; public competitive award.
disqualifiers: Issue codes are broad; a shared client name does not connect lobbying to the contract decision.
evidence: Client identity, lobbying period and subject, tender and decision records.
next_check: Read the lobbying subject and contract scope side by side.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A material public supplier is identified by an award record.
expected: A court source may contain a case naming the same party and disputing performance or solvency during the contract.
basis: Documented contract disputes can inform delivery-risk questions; court involvement is not a finding against a supplier.
outcome: A relevant adverse judgment, insolvency order or substantiated delivery dispute warrants checking public contract safeguards.
ordinary: Plaintiff rather than defendant; dismissed claim; unrelated dispute; settlement; historic case.
disqualifiers: Party name alone and allegations in pleadings are insufficient; determine role, status and legal entity.
evidence: Docket, operative judgment, contract performance obligations and recipient identity.
next_check: Read the docket status and party role before downloading a large case file.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A public award or grant names a recipient and purpose.
expected: An asset or licence record may show the recipient’s relevant operating project or holding.
basis: Comparing funded purpose with the actual asset can identify delivery or eligibility questions, without assuming all asset records are complete.
outcome: A verified mismatch between the funded project and its owner, status or location merits reading milestones.
ordinary: Parent versus subsidiary; project renamed; phase-specific award; administrative delay.
disqualifiers: Do not infer non-delivery from a missing register entry or compare unrelated projects owned by the same conglomerate.
evidence: Award scope and milestones, project crosswalk, historical asset status, delivery evidence.
next_check: Confirm the exact funded project and the record’s owner/operator role.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A charity filing names a grantee, contractor or officer in a material transaction.
expected: A company/ownership source may establish whether that counterparty was related to the charity’s decision makers.
basis: Related-party transactions can warrant governance scrutiny even when permitted and disclosed.
outcome: Verified control or personal role connecting decision makers to a paid counterparty merits reviewing disclosure and approval.
ordinary: Independent common-name party; arm’s-length transaction; disclosed related party; unrelated director dates.
disqualifiers: A shared agent address is not a related party; verify applicable disclosure duties separately.
evidence: Schedules, contracts, conflict disclosures, dated corporate roles and approval records.
next_check: Check identity and role dates for the named counterparty.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A company receives a material publicly disclosed award or subsidy.
expected: Issuer filings may describe the same award, associated project or financial effect in a compatible period.
basis: Reconciling public awards and company accounts can reveal disputed amounts or hidden dependency; obligations and revenues differ.
outcome: An unexplained material reconciliation difference merits checking accounting notes and award amendments.
ordinary: Accrual timing; parent consolidation; currency; fiscal-year boundaries; contingent awards.
disqualifiers: No omission claim without coverage and materiality analysis; never equate obligations to revenue.
evidence: Award transaction history, full financial notes, consolidation perimeter, currency basis.
next_check: Determine how the award should be recognized before comparing totals.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A disclosure names a client or foreign principal.
expected: A dated ownership source may identify a controlling interest not obvious from the client’s name.
basis: Tracing who benefits from representation gives context for a public policy campaign.
outcome: Verified undisclosed-to-the-reader ownership changes the interpretation of the represented interest.
ordinary: Disclosed ownership elsewhere; holding company; minority shareholder; outdated record.
disqualifiers: Do not call ownership legally undisclosed without identifying a reporting duty and coverage.
evidence: Client identity, original disclosure, dated control/ownership edges.
next_check: Follow one documented ownership edge and verify its meaning.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A recorded donation identifies an entity donor or a person with a documented company role.
expected: Ownership sources may connect nominally separate donors at the contribution date.
basis: Grouping actual related donors can show concentrated financial influence while preserving individual legal status.
outcome: A concentration hidden by nominal donor names warrants checking legal treatment and decision-maker connections.
ordinary: Independent relatives or employees; lawful corporate group donations; historic ownership.
disqualifiers: Do not aggregate employees’ donations as employer spending or infer coordination from a shared address.
evidence: Donor legal identity, beneficial ownership/role history, transaction-level donations/refunds.
next_check: Check whether the relevant jurisdiction permits the donor type before interpreting totals.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: An organization discloses lobbying on a regulation or policy area.
expected: An enforcement source may document findings against that same entity involving the policy area.
basis: A regulated party’s public influence efforts and enforcement history create a focused accountability question.
outcome: A material effort to change a rule implicated by a verified finding merits reading the proposed change.
ordinary: Lobbying for stricter standards; unrelated subsidiary; remedied matter; neutral technical input.
disqualifiers: No causal claim without decision records; identify final finding rather than allegation.
evidence: Lobbying subject and dates, operative enforcement finding, proposal text.
next_check: Check that the issue and enforcement matter concern the same conduct.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A grant describes funded clinical research and its institution or investigator.
expected: A trial registry may identify the corresponding study through grant references, sponsor, investigator and protocol.
basis: A matched study allows checking whether promised research milestones were achieved; dates and reporting duties vary.
outcome: A verified overdue or materially changed milestone merits asking the funder and sponsor for its explanation.
ordinary: Extension; nonclinical grant; different protocol; approved amendment; inapplicable reporting requirement.
disqualifiers: Institution name alone does not identify a trial; do not claim legally late results without trial category and rule verification.
evidence: Grant abstract/terms, protocol crosswalk, full registry history, extensions.
next_check: Find a shared protocol or grant reference in one study record.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A registered trial has prespecified outcomes and study dates.
expected: A publication matched by NCT/protocol reference can be compared with that prespecification.
basis: Outcome changes after data collection can affect interpretation; changes may be disclosed and justified.
outcome: An unexplained change in primary outcome or population merits checking protocol amendments and authors’ account.
ordinary: Prospective amendment; secondary analysis; multiple papers; indexing lag.
disqualifiers: DOI or author overlap alone does not identify a trial; abstracts cannot settle full reporting consistency.
evidence: Registration history, protocol, full article, statistical analysis plan and amendment dates.
next_check: Check the article’s explicit trial identifier before comparing outcomes.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A public grant identifies a research institution and technical project.
expected: Patent records may identify the resulting invention via acknowledgments, inventors and technical subject.
basis: Public support and private ownership of an invention can raise a concrete public-return question.
outcome: Verified publicly funded invention assigned away from the funded institution merits checking grant and license terms.
ordinary: Legitimate commercialization; inventor’s unrelated research; continuation family; assignment recorded late.
disqualifiers: Institution or inventor name alone cannot connect a patent to the grant; no rights violation presumed.
evidence: Grant scope, patent family, funding acknowledgments, assignment chain and grant IP terms.
next_check: Read one patent’s funding statement and assignment dates.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A disclosed payment identifies a physician, company and product.
expected: A registered trial may identify that physician or institution in research on the company’s product.
basis: Financial ties can matter to interpretation of evidence; they do not establish bias or a disclosure breach.
outcome: A verified investigator tie merits comparing published conflict declarations and the payment category.
ordinary: Research payment to institution; consulting unrelated to trial; common name; already disclosed.
disqualifiers: Do not equate payment to personal income; confirm physician and trial role independently.
evidence: Payment record, investigator identity and dates, article conflict statement and payment taxonomy.
next_check: Separate research payments from general payments and check product correspondence.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A marketed drug record identifies company and ingredient.
expected: Trial records may describe relevant evidence for the ingredient and indicated population.
basis: A drug-product crosswalk provides a route to examining the evidentiary basis, not a measure of efficacy.
outcome: A verified mismatch between marketed claims and studied populations/outcomes merits reviewing regulator assessments.
ordinary: Different dosage/formulation; off-label use; trial outside indexed periods; generic relying on earlier evidence.
disqualifiers: No absence-of-evidence claim from a registry search alone; match ingredient, formulation and indication.
evidence: Product monograph, regulatory assessment, protocol and study results.
next_check: Compare the approved indication with the matched study’s enrollment criteria.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A facility report identifies pollutant emissions, location and reporting year.
expected: Independent plume observations can be compared only for the same pollutant, operating period and physically attributable source.
basis: Independent measurements may reveal reporting discrepancies; intermittent remote flux cannot be directly equated with annual reported mass.
outcome: A repeated material discrepancy surviving measurement and temporal reconciliation merits operator/regulator questions.
ordinary: Intermittent releases; neighboring source; wind; detection limits; different gases; model uncertainty.
disqualifiers: Quarantine any comparison with no common gas, compatible units, usable observations or source attribution.
evidence: Original report scope, plume retrieval quality, wind field, production history and uncertainty.
next_check: Confirm common gas and an observed plume that can be attributed to the facility.
temporal: Match plume observation time to operations; annualization requires representative sampling and uncertainty, not one overpass.

initial: A mapped industrial facility or hazardous site has a verified location and activity.
expected: Population/building layers can estimate people or settlements near the site at the relevant date.
basis: Proximity measures potential exposure and emergency-planning priorities; it does not establish exposure dose or harm.
outcome: Substantial nearby population and a documented hazard merit checking monitoring and emergency plans.
ordinary: Non-operating facility; population allocation error; barrier or prevailing wind; old census.
disqualifiers: No arbitrary radius as a toxic exposure model; buildings are not counted as people.
evidence: Site boundary and hazard, population vintage, uncertainty and a justified impact model.
next_check: Validate site location and settlement presence on a small area before estimating exposed population.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: An industrial asset has a mapped footprint and development date.
expected: A protected-area boundary and designation history can be overlaid with the actual asset footprint.
basis: Overlap identifies a land-use question; not every designation prohibits every industrial activity.
outcome: Verified overlapping activity after designation warrants checking permit conditions and governing protection.
ordinary: Boundary imprecision; grandfathered permit; multiple-use designation; non-operating project.
disqualifiers: Point-in-polygon is screening only; no illegality without dated legal boundary and rules.
evidence: Asset footprint, historic protected boundary, designation instrument, permits and exceptions.
next_check: Read the protected-area designation and validate actual industrial footprint.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A concession or land-right polygon and effective interval are identified.
expected: Dated vegetation-change observations can be compared inside and outside that polygon.
basis: Land cover changes within a right warrant checking activity and responsibility; a holder need not have caused change.
outcome: A verified cluster of change after the right began merits a permit and operator check.
ordinary: Fire; smallholder activity; seasonal classification; lawful clearance; old boundaries.
disqualifiers: Do not infer causation from overlap or create separate tests by changing arbitrary radii/years.
evidence: Historical right boundary, quality-screened change observations, activity attribution and permits.
next_check: Inspect a few change pixels and original imagery before calculating affected area.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A hazardous or critical facility has a verified footprint and relevant operating period.
expected: A flood/storm/reservoir dataset may document a physically connected hazard at that site.
basis: Exposure can threaten services or release contaminants, but coarse regional events cannot establish inundation.
outcome: Site-specific exposure merits checking defenses, incident records and emergency planning.
ordinary: Protective works; plant above flood level; regional event not local flooding; inactive site.
disqualifiers: Require hazard footprint/intensity appropriate to site; reservoir proximity alone is not a flood event.
evidence: Hazard model/event footprint, terrain, site defenses, incident records and uncertainty.
next_check: Check whether the hazard dataset actually resolves conditions at the site.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A high-consequence facility identifies its operator or owner.
expected: Ownership disclosures can connect that operator to a dated parent or controlling party.
basis: Corporate attribution enables accountability for a documented environmental risk while separating operator from parent.
outcome: A verified parent connection warrants checking group policies, liabilities and financial capacity for remediation.
ordinary: Contract operator; joint venture; recent disposal; accounting rather than legal parent.
disqualifiers: No parent liability inferred from ownership alone; ownership must overlap the event date.
evidence: Facility identity, operator agreement, dated ownership edges and relevant liability rules.
next_check: Confirm the facility’s operator and owner are not being conflated.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A land right defines a basin-connected activity area and dates.
expected: Surface-water observations can be checked for change near the activity using seasonally comparable periods.
basis: Water change may expose a high-consequence question but rainfall, dams and other users can explain it.
outcome: A robust change spatially and temporally linked to the activity merits hydrological investigation.
ordinary: Drought; seasonal water; upstream infrastructure; classification error; unrelated extraction.
disqualifiers: No causal inference without catchment model and comparison areas; land right alone proves no extraction.
evidence: Right history, water observations, rainfall, hydrology and activity evidence.
next_check: Check seasonal comparability and whether the right has actually been exercised.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A tailings facility has a documented location and downstream connection.
expected: Dam/reservoir data may identify downstream infrastructure affected by a plausible failure path.
basis: A cascading-risk hypothesis needs terrain and engineering evidence; simple proximity is insufficient.
outcome: Verified downstream dependence merits reviewing consequence classifications and emergency plans.
ordinary: Independent basins; containment; inactive structure; inaccurate coordinates.
disqualifiers: Require drainage connectivity and credible failure scenario before claiming a cascade.
evidence: Facility design, terrain, downstream infrastructure, emergency plans.
next_check: Check flow direction and whether the two structures are hydrologically connected.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A conflict or civilian-harm event has a dated location with uncertainty.
expected: Independent damage assessment may show physical change compatible with the event.
basis: Converging time/place evidence can corroborate destruction, not determine perpetrator or intent.
outcome: Verified damage to civilian infrastructure merits primary-source and witness follow-up.
ordinary: Other event; pre-existing damage; geocoding error; images collected long afterward.
disqualifiers: No perpetrator, weapon or casualty inference from damage imagery alone.
evidence: Event source, precise geolocation, pre/post imagery and assessment method.
next_check: Compare event uncertainty and image acquisition dates.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A conflict event or episode has a defined location and period.
expected: Displacement records may show compatible movement from that area afterward.
basis: Temporal and geographic association helps target reporting on civilian consequences; origin/destination and reporting lag matter.
outcome: An aligned displacement increase merits checking local events, routes and counting methods.
ordinary: Seasonal migration; disaster; survey-round change; duplicate stocks/flows.
disqualifiers: No causal claim or individual identification from aggregate populations.
evidence: Event chronology, displacement definitions and coverage, alternative hazards.
next_check: Check whether the displacement field measures a stock, new flow, or cumulative events.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A disaster or hazard observation has a dated footprint or intensity estimate.
expected: Population/settlement data can quantify a compatible area of potential exposure.
basis: Exposure estimation can prioritize response scrutiny but is not a death or damage estimate.
outcome: Large verified exposure merits checking warnings, response and actual impact.
ordinary: Outdated settlement; evacuation; coarse footprint; modeled population error.
disqualifiers: No count of casualties or residents from building count without validated conversion.
evidence: Hazard footprint, population vintage and uncertainty, evacuation/response records.
next_check: Check spatial resolution and whether the footprint represents observed or forecast hazard.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A conflict event affects a specified settlement or critical service area.
expected: Nighttime radiance may change afterward relative to suitable local baselines.
basis: Light loss can indicate service disruption, evacuation or destruction but not distinguish among them.
outcome: Persistent quality-screened radiance loss merits checking power/service continuity on the ground.
ordinary: Cloud; moonlight; season; curfew; sensor change; planned outage.
disqualifiers: Discard low-quality observations; no causal or population estimate from radiance alone.
evidence: Quality flags, pre/post comparable observations, event evidence and service records.
next_check: Inspect quality masks before measuring a change.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: An event threatens communications in a defined place and period.
expected: Independent network measurements may show service disruption in that footprint.
basis: Convergent network signals can establish an outage question; attribution to deliberate shutdown requires separate evidence.
outcome: A sustained, geographically consistent disruption merits checking operator statements and multiple measurement streams.
ordinary: Power failure; probe failure; routing maintenance; sampling bias; unrelated cable break.
disqualifiers: A missing measurement is not an outage; ASN location is not necessarily user location.
evidence: Raw measurement coverage, baseline, routing data and operator/authority evidence.
next_check: Check probe coverage and whether multiple independent signals agree.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: An aid project identifies an operating location, recipient and funding period.
expected: Conflict events may overlap the actual project footprint while it operated.
basis: Overlap can motivate delivery, safeguarding and adaptation questions; country-level coincidence is weak.
outcome: A verified nearby attack or armed control change merits checking delivery and protection arrangements.
ordinary: Project elsewhere in country; suspended activity; geocoding error; unrelated armed event.
disqualifiers: Require project-specific location and event precision; funding disbursement does not prove on-site delivery.
evidence: Project documents, precise sites/dates, event source and monitoring records.
next_check: Find a site-level project location before linking local events.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: An arms-transfer or licensing series identifies an exporter, destination, weapon category and period.
expected: Conflict records may document use of a compatible system or relevant violence in the destination after delivery.
basis: Exports and conflict can reveal end-use questions; national aggregates cannot trace a weapon or establish an embargo breach.
outcome: A verified delivery of a specifically implicated system warrants end-user and licensing-document review.
ordinary: License not used; equipment from another supplier; defensive use; delivery in another year.
disqualifiers: No country-level attribution to a named actor; identify actual system and transfer, not merely license value.
evidence: Delivery confirmation, weapon provenance, end-user certificate, incident evidence and applicable rules.
next_check: Determine whether the source records approvals, orders or actual deliveries.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: An exploited vulnerability has a specific CVE identifier and affected product.
expected: NVD can describe the same CVE, affected versions and related references.
basis: Joining exact CVEs can reveal products with documented exploitation that merit public-service exposure checks.
outcome: A public-interest service using a verified affected version warrants a responsible, nonintrusive patch-status inquiry.
ordinary: Product patched; version banner stale; mitigation; service not internet-exposed.
disqualifiers: No scanning, exploitation or breach claim; a CPE match alone does not prove vulnerable deployment.
evidence: CVE record, affected-version criteria, independently authorized inventory and mitigation evidence.
next_check: Read the affected versions and vendor advisory; use passive/authorized inventory only.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A network source maps an organization to a documented ASN and validity period.
expected: Network measurement sources may show an outage or routing anomaly affecting that ASN.
basis: Network attribution can identify who can explain a service disruption, not who caused it.
outcome: A sustained corroborated disruption at a critical operator merits checking resiliency and response.
ordinary: Routing transfer; anycast; monitoring gap; scheduled maintenance.
disqualifiers: No provider culpability from ownership mapping; require ASN namespace and dates.
evidence: Dated ASN assignment, measurement coverage, operator confirmation.
next_check: Verify the ASN’s dated assignment before correlating signals.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A public-interest domain has dated registration or delegation information.
expected: Certificate records may show issuance for that same domain over time.
basis: Changes can identify control or security questions but certificates do not prove operational control or compromise.
outcome: Unexpected issuance around a documented ownership transition warrants checking registrar and certificate history.
ordinary: Routine automated renewal; CDN; wildcard; reseller; redacted registrant.
disqualifiers: No intrusion or beneficial-owner claim from domain/certificate association alone.
evidence: Domain normalization, registration history, certificate chain and authorized owner account.
next_check: Confirm exact domain and wildcard scope before interpreting issuance.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: An institution has a poor access-to-information compliance measure in a stated year.
expected: An access-order source may show decisions involving the same institution and relevant issue.
basis: Aggregate delays and case-level findings can focus questions about persistent transparency barriers.
outcome: Repeated substantiated procedural problems warrant checking backlog causes and corrective action.
ordinary: Complex requests; small denominator; changed institution; decisions relate to earlier requests.
disqualifiers: Orders are selected appealed cases, not a representative sample of all requests.
evidence: Measure definition/denominator, original orders, institution identity and request dates.
next_check: Read one order’s reasoning and align the underlying request period.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: An extractive payment disclosure identifies company, government/payee, project, payment stream and year.
expected: A compatible EITI disclosure may report government receipts for the same payer/project and fiscal basis.
basis: Two-sided payment reconciliation can expose discrepancies without assuming evasion or theft.
outcome: An unexplained material difference after reconciling scope and timing merits checking receipts and consolidation.
ordinary: Cash versus accrual; currency; different project aggregation; parent versus subsidiary; thresholds.
disqualifiers: Reject if country/company/stream/year coverage is not common; no missing-payment conclusion without completeness evidence.
evidence: Both disclosure definitions, currency conversion, payer identifiers and payment receipts.
next_check: Check whether EITI covers that country, fiscal period and payment stream.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A sanctions entry identifies a person, entity or vessel and the restriction was in force on the relevant date.
expected: A corporate or leak record may name the same person as an officer, director or intermediary; corroborate the role with current official records.
basis: A dated governance role is a concrete accountability lead, but does not establish ownership or automatic blocking.
outcome: A verified continuing senior role or authorized signatory relationship merits checking activities and applicable restrictions.
ordinary: Former director; professional intermediary; namesake; leak snapshot is old; role ended before designation.
disqualifiers: First resolve actual identity and entity type; distinguish SDN blocking from non-SDN restrictions; establish the applicable jurisdiction, conduct, dates, program and authorizations/exceptions. A match alone establishes none of these. A director or intermediary is not necessarily an owner; historical leaked entries are leads requiring primary-source corroboration.
evidence: Official appointment and resignation history, identity evidence, actual activity, program rules and authorizations.
next_check: Determine whether the original record labels the person as officer, director, shareholder or intermediary; check effective role dates.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: Country-by-country statistics show profits and real activity concentrated differently across partner jurisdictions.
expected: Secrecy-index components may characterize the jurisdictions receiving unusually high profits relative to employees or assets.
basis: A mismatch motivates reporting on profit location, not an allegation against a company. Composite secrecy rankings are explanatory context, not causal instruments.
outcome: A robust profit/activity disparity merits checking tax rules, aggregate coverage and published corporate cases.
ordinary: Holding-company structures; losses; missing reporters; sector mix; double-counted profits.
disqualifiers: No actor-level tax evasion or causal claim from anonymized jurisdiction totals; preserve confidentiality thresholds.
evidence: Statistical coverage, tax definitions, sector mix, denominator and index component vintage.
next_check: Recompute one jurisdiction’s ratio using a compatible employee or tangible-asset denominator.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A bilateral commodity series records EU exports or imports for a specified product and period.
expected: The corresponding partner-side trade series may differ after harmonizing direction, valuation, classification and timing.
basis: Mirror gaps can identify measurement or trade-route questions; freight, re-exporting and valuation routinely create differences.
outcome: A persistent material residual after reconciliation merits inspecting customs methodology and specific routes.
ordinary: CIF versus FOB; lags; transit; re-exports; confidentiality; code revision; special trade systems.
disqualifiers: No firm-level misinvoicing or sanctions-evasion claim from aggregate discrepancies.
evidence: Both trade metadata, concordances, quantity/value units, partner definitions and revisions.
next_check: Select non-EU partner-reported Comtrade data against EU-reported Comext, not the same EU series redistributed in both; reconcile one product-month including valuation and re-export treatment.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: Regulated-bank data show a material concentration or change in an asset category.
expected: Investment-fund survey aggregates may show parallel exposure or liquidity changes in a compatible category and period.
basis: Co-movement may indicate system-wide exposure deserving scrutiny; two confidential aggregates do not identify counterparty links.
outcome: A compatible concentration in illiquid assets merits consulting stress-test assumptions and disclosure notes.
ordinary: Consolidation changes; valuation movements; survey population shifts; category mismatch.
disqualifiers: No bilateral institution-to-fund exposure inferred; schema and replacement OSFI service must be verified.
evidence: Both taxonomies, coverage, consolidation basis, valuation dates and published stress-test assumptions.
next_check: Check the current OSFI endpoint and align the asset-category definition before comparing values.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A contract award identifies a supplier’s legal entity and date.
expected: The competent company registry may establish that entity’s legal existence/status at the award date.
basis: An unresolved dissolved or non-existent supplier identity can signal a data or procurement problem; foreign registries are relevant only with a documented incorporation link.
outcome: A verified adverse legal-status interval overlapping actual new contracting warrants checking succession and contracting identity.
ordinary: Trading name; reactivation; successor; branch; registry lag; current status differs from historical status.
disqualifiers: No rule that every inactive status forbids all contracts is established; require historical official registry evidence and correct jurisdiction.
evidence: Contract recipient ID/jurisdiction, historical status extracts, successor documents and actual award action.
next_check: Establish incorporation jurisdiction before querying any registry; stop if it is outside that registry’s coverage.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: An ad archive identifies a political advertiser or disclaimer and a dated spend range.
expected: Political-finance records may identify the payer or affiliated campaign’s spending in a compatible reporting period.
basis: Reconciliation can reveal transparency questions, but platform ranges and statutory categories seldom map one-to-one.
outcome: An unexplained gap for a verified payer merits checking invoices, reporting thresholds and third-party rules.
ordinary: Range uncertainty; currency; agency buys; in-kind support; reporting lag; different ad categories.
disqualifiers: No unreported-spending claim without legal duty, full return coverage and reconciled payer identity.
evidence: Original ad record, payer verification, complete finance return, invoices and applicable rules.
next_check: Resolve disclaimer to actual payer and compare reporting periods before summing ranges.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A US lobbying or foreign-agent disclosure describes a specific policy request and period.
expected: Federal Register records may document the corresponding proposal, final rule or agency action.
basis: A documented request and later decision create a testable influence question; temporal order is not proof of causation.
outcome: A closely aligned rule change merits comparing draft text, comments, meetings and the agency’s stated basis.
ordinary: Broad industry agreement; pre-existing plan; court mandate; routine technical correction.
disqualifiers: Issue-category overlap is not a direct policy match; no quid-pro-quo inference.
evidence: Disclosure text, docket/RIN crosswalk, draft/final rule, comments and decision timeline.
next_check: Identify the exact docket or regulatory identifier in the client’s stated issue.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: An EU transparency disclosure names a client and specific legislative interest.
expected: EUR-Lex may document amendments or adopted text in that precise procedure.
basis: Text-level alignment can focus reporting on participation in lawmaking; multiple actors may independently support it.
outcome: A material requested change appearing in adopted text warrants tracing meetings and submissions.
ordinary: Public consultation; shared policy preference; multilingual wording; unrelated procedure.
disqualifiers: No causal attribution from timing or shared keywords; verify exact procedure and actor role.
evidence: Client disclosure, CELEX/procedure crosswalk, text versions, submissions and meeting evidence.
next_check: Resolve the legislative procedure before comparing exact requested language.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A Canadian lobbying disclosure identifies a specific proposed regulatory change.
expected: The Canada Gazette may contain the corresponding proposal or final instrument.
basis: A dated request and textual change can guide accountability reporting without proving capture.
outcome: An aligned material change merits examining the impact statement and consultation response.
ordinary: General policy agenda; court ruling; routine update; unrelated docket.
disqualifiers: Gazette feed metadata is only discovery; read authoritative instrument and commencement provisions.
evidence: Lobbying disclosure, full Gazette text, instrument identity, consultation and effective dates.
next_check: Find the actual instrument rather than relying on the feed title.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A federal travel/hospitality disclosure records an official, destination and purpose around a decision.
expected: Lobbying records may name that same official and an interest relevant to the disclosed trip.
basis: A corroborated meeting can reveal access around decisions; co-location alone does not establish a meeting.
outcome: A verified engagement relevant to a decision warrants checking calendar records and official rationale.
ordinary: Routine delegation; different dates; generic purpose; namesake official; no actual meeting.
disqualifiers: No lobbying non-disclosure allegation from absence in the register without scope and completeness evidence.
evidence: Travel claim, official identity and role dates, lobbying entry, calendar or meeting confirmation.
next_check: Compare dates, role and purpose, then request the narrow calendar entry.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: An aircraft registry identifies a tail number, serial number and owner for a public-interest aircraft.
expected: Transponder observations may show dated activity for that aircraft after an authoritative ICAO-address/registration crosswalk.
basis: A documented aircraft trip can test public travel or asset-use claims; it cannot identify passengers or purpose.
outcome: A verified itinerary inconsistent with a specific public account merits flight-plan and operator questions.
ordinary: Tail reuse; leasing; maintenance; owner not passenger; receiver gaps.
disqualifiers: A callsign or transponder address alone is not an owner/passenger identity; no absence claims from missing tracks.
evidence: Registration history, serial/ICAO mapping, track quality and independent flight/owner evidence.
next_check: Resolve registration and transponder identity at the flight date.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A transport occurrence names a vehicle/vessel/aircraft and operator at the incident date.
expected: The relevant registry may establish the legal owner or registration history at that time.
basis: Operator/owner distinctions can identify who should answer safety or maintenance questions.
outcome: Repeated documented occurrences involving a verified owner/operator merit a safety-system review.
ordinary: Lease operator differs; ownership changed; different aircraft with reused tail; occurrence not causal finding.
disqualifiers: Match transport mode and vehicle namespace first; no owner culpability inferred from registration.
evidence: Occurrence report, investigation status, dated registry entry, operator/maintenance agreement.
next_check: Check whether the occurrence concerns air or marine transport before selecting registry.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A land deal identifies a project area, investor and claimed agricultural use.
expected: Compatible crop or evapotranspiration products may test the claimed cultivated area or water use during operations.
basis: Remote indicators can challenge project claims but are modelled and geography-specific; a deal may never have been implemented.
outcome: A robust mismatch between documented promised/actual cultivation and observations merits field and permit checks.
ordinary: Fallow cycle; crop rotation; product vintage; model spread; project delays; mixed pixels.
disqualifiers: Require actual field boundary and product coverage; do not equate evapotranspiration to unlawful extraction.
evidence: Project terms, crop calendar, product methods/uncertainty and local operational evidence.
next_check: Check product geography and the project’s actual operating dates.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A facility with a documented relevant pollutant operates near an air-quality monitor.
expected: Quality-controlled station observations may show a pollutant anomaly during compatible operating and wind conditions.
basis: A nearby reading supports an exposure question but source attribution needs dispersion, other emitters and weather.
outcome: A reproducible downwind anomaly merits checking permit limits and independent monitoring.
ordinary: Traffic; wildfire; other plant; calibration; stagnant weather; changed monitor.
disqualifiers: Do not identify a polluter from proximity or claim permit breach from ambient concentrations alone.
evidence: Monitor QA, common pollutant, meteorology, operation logs and competing-source inventory.
next_check: Check monitor calibration and wind direction for one episode.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A machine-detected waste-site candidate has a mapped footprint and confidence score.
expected: A protected-area layer may place the candidate within a dated designation boundary.
basis: Potential waste disposal in sensitive land is worth verification; detection is not proof of waste, operator or illegality.
outcome: A ground/imagery-confirmed waste site inside a relevant protected boundary merits permit and cleanup inquiries.
ordinary: Recycling stockpile; bare ground false positive; boundary error; permitted use; old imagery.
disqualifiers: Human verification of detection and legal designation required before naming a polluter or alleging illegal dumping.
evidence: Original imagery, quality flags, historical boundary, on-site/official confirmation and permits.
next_check: Inspect the candidate image and precise protection boundary before investigating operators.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A federal contaminated-site record identifies a known or suspected hazard and location.
expected: Compatible population or settlement layers may identify communities near the site.
basis: Proximity can prioritize questions about testing and remediation; site status does not measure actual exposure.
outcome: Verified potentially affected nearby communities merit checking contaminant pathways and remediation milestones.
ordinary: Suspected rather than confirmed contamination; completed cleanup; migration; local barriers.
disqualifiers: Inventory is federal-only; buildings are not people and proximity is not dose.
evidence: Site status history, contaminant/pathway data, population vintage, remediation plan.
next_check: Read site classification and the latest investigation status before estimating population.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A proposed or operating facility has a dated footprint affecting habitat.
expected: Species occurrence records may document sensitive taxa within a scientifically justified impact area before or during development.
basis: Verified occurrences can inform environmental-assessment scrutiny; opportunistic observations cannot establish complete biodiversity.
outcome: A confirmed relevant occurrence omitted from a scoped assessment merits checking survey methods and species protections.
ordinary: Obscured coordinates; misidentified taxon; outdated occurrence; seasonal use; outside impact pathway.
disqualifiers: No absence inference; no exact public disclosure of sensitive species locations; legal protection must be independently checked.
evidence: Occurrence provenance, taxonomic validation, coordinate uncertainty, assessment scope and impact pathway.
next_check: Check occurrence uncertainty and original observation before overlaying it on the project.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A damaging weather-related event has a verified location and onset.
expected: A contemporaneously archived forecast may show the warning available before that event.
basis: Forecast versus response timing can guide preparedness questions, accounting for probabilities and changing information.
outcome: A credible early forecast plus delayed documented action merits checking decision logs and warning delivery.
ordinary: Forecast uncertainty; last-minute track change; insufficient infrastructure; warnings issued through other channels.
disqualifiers: Restrict to forecastable weather events; ECMWF rolling archive cannot reconstruct old forecasts unless independently archived.
evidence: Time-stamped pre-event forecast, probability/lead time, dissemination and response chronology.
next_check: Locate a preserved forecast issued before onset; stop if only hindsight reanalysis exists.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A geolocated aid project identifies a funding amount, sector and period.
expected: Compatible relative-wealth estimates or election returns may show how funding is distributed across local communities.
basis: Comparisons can test allocation equity or apparent political concentration, controlling for need and eligible population.
outcome: A robust allocation disparity warrants checking criteria, project placement and local decision records.
ordinary: Need-based targeting; implementation costs; geography mismatch; model bias; older election.
disqualifiers: Do not infer patronage causally or treat relative wealth as income; electoral and population denominators must be valid.
evidence: Precise project sites, amounts, eligibility/needs measures, boundary concordance and allocation rules.
next_check: Validate project coordinates and decide whether the outcome is need-adjusted aid allocation, not just raw totals.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.

initial: A party manifesto makes a specific measurable commitment before an election.
expected: Cabinet records can establish when that party actually held relevant governing authority.
basis: Authority and timing are prerequisites for testing a broken-promise claim; coalition compromises matter.
outcome: A verified governing interval allows a narrowly specified follow-up against implementation records.
ordinary: Coalition veto; regional versus national power; changed party identity; vague promise.
disqualifiers: No failure claim from manifesto/cabinet data alone; an additional official implementation outcome is required.
evidence: Original pledge text, party/cabinet crosswalk, portfolio powers, coalition agreement and implementation record.
next_check: Check whether the party controlled the relevant policy portfolio.
temporal: Align event dates and effective intervals; use historical snapshots, not current status projected backward.
